claims: At unit viscosity, for every finite M>0 there is epsilon(M)>0: a local suitable weak pair defined near the closure of Q1 with A(1)+E(1)+D(1)<=M and integral_Q1 dist_F(grad u,all rank<=1 matrices)^2<epsilon(M) is regular at the terminal centre. No smooth-preterminal hypothesis is used.

Strong velocity L2/L3 and weak gradient L2 compactness pass the second gradient minors distributionally. The cofactor estimate gives rank<=1 in the limit, without strong gradients or convex lower semicontinuity of the nonconvex distance.

Tracefree rank-one gradients give harmonic pressure. Its time-integrated gradient is spatially smooth and bounded on smaller fixed cylinders. The corrected velocity solves a solenoidal forced equation with an L2 right hand side.

An explicit adaptation of O'Leary's small-power truncation, not direct invocation of its pressure-gradient theorem, gives three strict integrability gains 10/3 to 15/4 to 9/2 to 21/4 and C_limit(r)<=K_u*r^(1/7), uniformly up to the backward top.

Fixed spatial Riesz decomposition has a strongly converging near part and uniformly bounded harmonic remainders. The limiting near part is also harmonic. Their uncentered pressure integral decays O(r), enabling fixed-r then n-to-infinity transfer to the original suitable solutions and a fixed CKN threshold.

limitations: Arbitrary NS evolution producing a prescribed-centre scale with both a controlled energy/pressure cap and square-defect smaller than epsilon(M) remains unproved.
No computable epsilon(M), defect-to-radius modulus, optimal assumptions or complete novelty audit is provided.
Finite unnormalized dissipation does not automatically control r^(-1) times local dissipation or square defect. Nested-cylinder lower bounds cannot be summed as independent costs.
General unforced 3D global regularity, a singularity construction, and the Clay goal remain open.
Participating AI review is not human peer review or a complete novelty certification.
